payload.prompt: We sent an invoice for 13833 EUR to Brightstone Ltd (org no. 883627393) when the exchange rate was 11.86 NOK/EUR. The customer has now paid, but the rate is 12.74 NOK/EUR. Register the payment and post the exchange rate difference (agio) to the correct account.

payload.goal: Register payment from Brightstone Ltd for invoice of 13833 EUR, and post the exchange rate gain (agio) arising from the difference between the invoice rate (11.86 NOK/EUR) and the payment rate (12.74 NOK/EUR) to the correct currency gain/loss account.
likely_resources: Currency account or exchange rate settings
Voucher/journal entry for exchange rate difference
success_checks: Invoice of 13833 EUR is marked as fully paid in Tripletex
Payment registered at rate 12.74 NOK/EUR (NOK received = 13833 × 12.74 = 176,212.42 NOK)
Invoice was originally booked at 11.86 NOK/EUR (13833 × 11.86 = 164,039.38 NOK)
Exchange rate gain (agio) = 176,212.42 - 164,039.38 = 12,173.04 NOK posted to account 8060 (Agio) or equivalent
Voucher/journal entry created for the agio difference with correct debit/credit entries
Customer ledger balance for Brightstone Ltd is zero after payment
No open receivables remain on the invoice
risk_notes: Invoice date and payment date not explicitly provided — needed for correct period posting and exchange rate documentation
Tripletex may auto-calculate agio if multi-currency is enabled and payment is registered in EUR; verify whether manual journal entry is needed or system handles it automatically
Confirm which bank account (NOK or EUR) the payment was received into — affects how the agio entry is structured
If payment received in EUR and converted by bank, the NOK amount credited may differ slightly from 12.74 rate — use actual bank statement amount
Agio account number may vary by chart of accounts setup (commonly 8060 in Norwegian standard); verify correct account
Multi-currency module must be enabled in Tripletex for EUR invoicing and automatic agio handling
Organization number 883627393 must match an existing or newly created customer record
VAT treatment on agio: currency gains are typically VAT-exempt (financial income) — ensure no VAT is applied to the agio posting
payload.suggested_first_action: Verify that the multi-currency module is enabled in Tripletex and that Brightstone Ltd exists as a customer; then locate the open EUR invoice for 13833 EUR and register payment at 12.74 NOK/EUR.

line_items.description: Invoice payment – 13833 EUR at invoice rate 11.86 NOK/EUR
Agio (exchange rate gain) – difference between payment rate 12.74 and invoice rate 11.86 NOK/EUR on 13833 EUR

ordered_steps: 1. Enable multi-currency module in Tripletex (Settings → Modules) if not already active
2. Verify or create customer Brightstone Ltd with org no. 883627393 via POST /customer
3. Locate the open EUR invoice for 13833 EUR issued to Brightstone Ltd via GET /invoice (filter by customer and currency)
4. Register payment on the invoice via POST /invoice/{id}/payment with amount=13833 EUR, currency=EUR, exchange rate=12.74, payment date=<actual payment date>
5. Confirm whether Tripletex auto-posts the agio difference (12,173.04 NOK) to account 8060; if not, proceed to step 6
6. Create a manual journal voucher via POST /ledger/voucher with the following entries:
- Debit: Accounts Receivable (1500) 12,173.04 NOK (to clear the rate difference on the receivable)
7. Verify customer ledger balance for Brightstone Ltd is zero via GET /ledger/account (filter customer 883627393)
8. Confirm invoice status is 'PAID' via GET /invoice/{id}
9. Reconcile bank account to confirm NOK receipt matches 176,212.42 NOK (or actual bank amount)

Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.

rules: Use ?number=XXXX to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
Do NOT use other query params — they are not supported.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
POSTING BALANCE RULES (which determines single-leg vs manual-leg):
vatType != 0 (e.g. id=3 for 25%): include ONLY the debit posting with GROSS amount. Tripletex auto-generates VAT + credit.
vatType == 0 (exempt): include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': you used vatType=0 but only one posting. Either add the credit posting manually OR change to the correct vatType (e.g. 3 for 25%).
NEVER default to vatType=0 for standard purchases — use vatType=3 (25%) unless explicitly VAT-exempt.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.
